themes.paper: Base palette in @theme (src/index.css). Print inherits it and rebinds paper and panel to #ffffff.
themes.night: Screen-only override: @media screen { :root:not([data-theme="light"]) }. Frontmatter keys ending in -night.

display.purpose: View headings, heavy sentence case. Print headings run 30px.

readout.purpose: The live dragged value over the stage, in ballpoint ink.

body-sm.purpose: Descriptions, button text and table cells.

label.purpose: Field labels, rule-label section heads and chips.

caption.purpose: Summary labels, phone tab labels and units.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Overlays on the stage, such as the readout and demo captions.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: A cut sheet lying on the cuadrícula.

motion.name: rise
motion.value: rise 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both; from opacity 0, translateY(6px)

motion.name: readout-hold
motion.purpose: How long the live readout lingers after the last change.

cuadricula.scope: Work stages only: cut sheets, bar plans and the 3D floor.

extensions.knownDivergence: The Expo iOS app (mobile/) still carries the previous "taller nocturno" palette and fonts. It is out of scope for this system until it is ported.

narrative.overview:
The planner is a maker's grid notebook. Every measurement sits on one true-scale cuadrícula, and whatever the maker is working on right now (the active step, the hovered piece, the size being dragged) is swept with a yellow highlighter. The page is notebook-white paper in daylight and ink-blue paper at night. Both themes are first-class. The paper palette is the base and the one print inherits; the night notebook overrides it on screen only.

The density is that of a well-kept notebook page. A 340 px rail of grouped controls sits beside a large stage, cut and order tables run edge to edge in ruled modules, and hairlines (1 px) do the structuring. Ink colours carry meaning and nothing is decorative: ballpoint blue is what you chose or can press, margin red is where you cut or what is wrong, the highlighter is where you are. Numbers are the product, so every measurement is set in a tabular monospace and is the most legible thing on the screen.

The world rejects the category default (a dark CAD stage beside a neutral settings panel) and the "taller nocturno" dark-shop costume it replaced: no amber-on-graphite, no condensed uppercase display, no hard red offset shadows.
keyCharacteristics: Two paper palettes (day and night) on one set of tokens. Components read tokens and never branch on theme.
The true-scale cuadrícula (20 px cells, a stronger line every 100 px) on work stages only.
Three inks with fixed jobs: ballpoint (accent), margin red (cut), highlighter (hi).
Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for words and Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono for numbers.
Hairline rules, 6–16 px radii, and low, soft shadows only on things that float.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Ballpoint is for what you chose or can press. Margin red is for cuts, errors and invalid states, plus the notebook's one margin rule. The highlighter is for where you are right now: the active step or piece and the dimension being dragged. No ink is ever used for decoration.

rules.name: The Ink-Token Rule
rules.body: Coloured text always uses the `-ink` token (`accent-ink`, `cut-ink`), never the fill token, because only the ink values hold 5:1 in both themes.

rules.name: The Two-Palette Rule
rules.body: A new colour token goes into both the `@theme` block and the screen-only night override, never into print. WebGL cannot read CSS variables, so Viewer3D's PALETTE mirrors the palette per theme and is the only place a component knows the theme.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Measurement Rule
rules.body: The mono face is only for numbers, measurements and piece codes (L1, A2). Words, sentences and labels are set in the sans, even when they sit in a numeric table.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase tracked labels anywhere. Hierarchy comes from weight and size, and section heads are bold sentence case followed by a hairline.

rules.name: The 11 px Floor
rules.body: No screen text is under 11px. The 11px size is reserved for slider bounds and fine print. Only the print report goes smaller (10px table heads).

rules.name: The Soft-Only Rule
rules.body: Shadows have a zero x-offset, at most a 2px y-offset and a blur at least as large as that offset. No hard offset shadows and no glows. Selection is drawn with ink (border, wash, fill), never with a shadow.

dos: Do use ballpoint (`accent`) for selection and primary actions, and `accent-ink` whenever that blue is text.
Do use the highlighter (`hi`) only for the active step or piece and the dimension being dragged, always under #141a2b text.
Do keep margin red (`cut`) for cuts, errors and invalid states. The 1 px rail margin rule is the one structural use.
Do set every number and measurement in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with tabular figures.
Do put the cuadrícula (`.stage-grid`) on work stages only: cut sheets, bar plans and the 3D floor.
Do add every new colour token to both the paper `@theme` block and the night override, and mirror it in Viewer3D's PALETTE if WebGL needs it.
Do keep screen text at 11px or larger and every text pair at 5:1 or better in both themes.
donts: Don't use hard offset shadows; shadows stay soft, short and graphite-tinted.
Don't put coloured side stripes on callouts; errors use a full red wash with a line icon.
Don't use uppercase tracked labels or eyebrow kickers; section heads are bold sentence case with a hairline.
Don't set words or sentences in the mono face.
Don't use red for focus, selection or emphasis.
Don't colour text with a fill token (`accent`, `cut`); use the `-ink` token.
Don't lay the cuadrícula behind forms, lists or chrome.
Don't read the theme in a component; read tokens.
